- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is above recent mean, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, cap the overshoot at +15% above prior peak to prevent overcorrection.  
- If true outcome consistently lags forecast by 2–3 days, adjust forward-looking models to reduce early peak bias.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is rising, apply mean reversion: subtract 2–5% from forecast to avoid false momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to align with mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.4→0.7) and forecast is flat, increase forecast by 2–3% to reflect sentiment momentum.
